summary: Cinder block cabin at 2,516 m in southwestern Alberta that replaced a 1954 cabin in 1978; register lists it active with access mode fly, while a 2007 trip report describes a road.

facts.design: Cinder block cabin built on the ground

access.note: Register lists access mode as fly and the lookout as active. A 2007 trip report describes driving a rough road part of the way. No source describes public visits today.

corrections.why: Register lists the lookout as active with access mode fly. No source says it is closed to visitors, so restricted is the level the sources support.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register gives access mode fly; a 2007 trip report describes a rough road drivable part of the way and a short walk up a ridge. Both are reported in the story and neither is treated as the sole answer.

sources.title: Wildfire Lookouts of Alberta (WF_WILDFIRE_LOOKOUT), FIRES database extract

notes_for_editor: Register confirms the 1978 cabin, cabin type, 2.0 m height and 2,516 m elevation; it is kept as recorded even though a height figure is unusual for a cabin. The 1954 cabin and the 1978 replacement rest on one secondary history page that cites Mike Potter's 1998 hiking guide, which was not checked. Access 'restricted' is an editorial level from working status; no source states a public access rule. The register (fly) and the 2007 trip report (road) disagree and the story says so. Brief's access 'closed' is not supported by a source that says the site is closed. Excluded: a Washington State Sugarloaf Mountain lookout page from firelookout.com, a different site. A YouTube result seen only as a search snippet calls Sugarloaf Mountain south-east Alberta; it conflicts with the register and the blog and was not used.
